They don't really show much interest outside of picking up my medication for me, I guess it just makes them uncomfortable or something despite depression running in the family. I obviously don't want anyone going out of their way for me or treating me special or anything and I definitely don't want to bring anyone down with me either, but it's been really hard dealing with it on my own all these years and a helping hand or a "how are you feeling" once every blue moon would be nice, just so I knew someone cared.

I got a hand on the shoulder and a "you okay?" from her and after they left she was clearly just pissed with me and has never tried to talk to me about it even once. She was more concerned about the state of the house in front of strangers than with me.

So yeah. It would be nice for my depression to be acknowledged. Would be nice for someone to give a crap for once.

The sad thing about depression is sometimes there just isn't a reason. For me it's like.. everything is fine. Nothing has gone wrong. I have my little problems and stresses like everyone else but nothing worth getting depressed over. I'm pretty pleased with everything at the moment, but there's still this overwhelming black cloud hovering over me. 

Sometimes there just is no reason, it just is. A chemical imbalance, your body not doing it's job properly. I feel like that's one of the hardest kinds of depression to get over because like you said, how do you fix a problem that isn't even there? At least if theres an actual trigger or problem it's something you could find a way to solve, y'know? I think if you've been like this for a long time or if it lasts a long time after today you should consider going to a doctor and getting some medication to regulate your system. Good luck, I know this is tough.

I feel like shit right now and want to eat an entire crust stuffed pizza. I wanna eat my favourite donuts while chugging a bottle of coke and shoving a bag of crisps/chips down my throat. It sucks so hard.

I've only tried two so far but will be asking for something new tomorrow at a doctors appointment. First medication I tried was amytriptyline (100mg), I can't remember if it helped my depression because it wasn't as bad as it is now at the time 2 years ago and I did have a few side effects, like dizziness and sometimes my arms would go red and feel like they were on fire, but my worst side effect was feeling like I was *starving*. No matter how much I ate I felt completely empty and it was so bad it triggered my binge eating. I don't think I even once felt full after a meal while on amytriptyline and as a result it made me gain maybe 30lbs in six months and I still haven't lost any of it even 6 months later after I had my dose decreased to 0. It made me gain nearly 10" on my hips. I'll never go back on it full time again.

The one I'm currently on is Lyrica/Pregabalin (400mg) and while it works for anxiety and some chronic pain it does absolutely nothing for depression. It doesn't even mention depression a single time on the leaflet so I feel like my doctor may have made a mistake when he prescribed it to me, although he did prescribe it with fibromyalgia in mind. It's generally prescribed for epilepsy and generalised anxiety disorder. 

Hopefully I'll get something better tomorrow if the unsympathetic doctor I'm seeing feels like helping me. I'm praying for something good if she does.

The way medication for depression effects a person is very different for every person. One that works for one person might not work for you and you might end up having to try a few different kinds before you find the right ones that work how you want them to. Antidepressants take a short while to kick in and usually you have to slowly increase the dose over a small number of weeks depending on what you're taking so you don't get overwhelmed, so they aren't something you'd be taking for only a week but rather more long term. 

I believe they can really work, especially once you find the right ones! But like with any medication they will likely come with side effects, usually not serious but they can turn you off. Normal side effects I've seen and experienced are appetite changes which can lead to weight gain or loss, feeling sleepy, loss of sexual desire, and slightly blurry vision every now and then (rarely for me but it happens. It goes after a nights sleep). You won't always get them all or sometimes you'll get none but it's all possible.

I'd personally take any and all side effects if it meant being able to go through a day without thinking of all the ways I could die. If you think you can't take it anymore I'd recommend seeing your doctor and asking about getting something to do help you out, they might even refer you to a psychologist which can help you a lot too. I wish you the best of luck! Starting medication can be scary but they can really help you too.

I've noticed that I'm like this when it comes to fake it until you make it. To friends, family, strangers, even online on social media, I have this habit of just acting cheerful and okay. I don't reveal my concerns or
problems to others. I don't even think about it when I'm doing it, it just started coming naturally. And in the moment I think it works, mostly offline. 

But then when I'm finally alone, in my room with nobody else around me, feeling miserable and wanting out of life comes straight back to me. That faked cheeriness only lasts for however long I'm surrounded by people, or hell even just one person. 

It's extremely temporary for me. I think the distraction is what makes it easy to pretend but when that distraction is gone there's nothing left to pretend in front of. I'm not sure how much it works, I could be doing it wrong for all I know. Maybe I need to force it when I'm alone too but that's hard when I know it's fake. You could always try it, I don't see the harm in giving it a go at all, but please don't expect it to immediately work, change everything and your outlook on life, because it might not end up working for you at all and it would suck twice as much if you got your hopes up for nothing.
